title: Leh to Leh via Umling La (7N/8D)
reportingPoint: The trip starts and ends in Leh. Our representative receives you on arrival in Leh, and group pickup and drop are included. Reporting details are shared once your booking is confirmed.
highlights: Ride over Khardung La to Nubra Valley
Night in camps at Pangong Tso
Pangong to Hanle through Lukung and Chushul
Hanle Observatory of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics
Day ride from Hanle to Umling La and back
overview:
A Ladakh road trip that goes beyond the usual circuit: Leh, Nubra Valley, Pangong Tso, Hanle, Umling La and Tso Moriri. It is a **7 Nights / 8 Days** group trip that starts and ends in Leh; it does not start from Delhi, so you make your own way to Leh. You can ride your own bike, ride a rented bike solo or as a pair, or travel in an SUV or tempo traveller. Plan to reach Leh at least one day before the trip starts so that you complete the 48 hours of acclimatisation the government SOPs ask for.

Day 1 is for arriving and acclimatising in Leh. Day 2 crosses Khardung La to Nubra Valley, with stops at Diskit Monastery and the Hunder sand dunes. Day 3 runs from Nubra to Pangong Tso for a night in camps by the lake. Day 4 is the 8 to 9 hour drive to Hanle through Lukung and Chushul, with a visit to the Hanle Observatory. Day 5 is the ride to Umling La and back to Hanle. Day 6 goes to Tso Moriri via Nyoma and the Mahe bridge, Day 7 returns to Leh, and Day 8 is departure. Stays are in hotels, camps, cottages and homestays on triple sharing, with a backup vehicle, a mechanic, inner line permits and an oxygen cylinder along. Batches run from May to early September. Prices start at ₹19,000 per person for the Own Bike option on triple sharing (5% GST extra).

itinerary.title: Arrival at Leh
itinerary.content:
Arrive in Leh, where our representative welcomes you.
Today is for acclimatising to the cold and the altitude.
Overnight stay at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Leh to Nubra Valley via Khardung La
itinerary.content:
After breakfast, set off for Nubra Valley.
Ride over Khardung La and spend some time at the top.
Ride to Diskit Monastery for a view over Nubra Valley.
Stop at the Hunder sand dunes, known for double-humped camel rides in the cold desert.
Dinner and overnight stay at camps or cottages.

itinerary.title: Nubra to Pangong Tso
itinerary.content:
After breakfast, leave Nubra Valley for Pangong Tso.
Arrive at Pangong Tso in the late afternoon. The lake is known for changing colour several times a day.
Spend the evening by the lake, with snow-capped mountains around it.
Dinner and overnight stay at camps at Pangong.

itinerary.title: Pangong Tso to Hanle
itinerary.content:
After breakfast, leave for the small village of Hanle, an offbeat destination in the Changthang region close to the Indo-China border.
It is an 8 to 9 hour drive from Pangong, passing through Lukung and the Chushul Valley.
Reach Hanle in the evening and visit the Chandra Telescope (Hanle Observatory) of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.
Check in at the homestay or hotel and have a Ladakhi dinner.
Overnight stay in Hanle.

itinerary.title: Hanle to Umling La and back
itinerary.content:
After breakfast, ride towards Umling La, known as one of the highest motorable roads in the world.
Spend time at the top for photographs.
Ride back and reach Hanle by evening.
Dinner and overnight stay in Hanle.

itinerary.title: Hanle to Tso Moriri
itinerary.content:
After breakfast, leave for Tso Moriri lake (14,000 ft), passing Nyoma and the Mahe bridge on the way.
The landscape keeps changing through the ride until you reach the lake.
Dinner and overnight stay at the campsite.

itinerary.title: Tso Moriri to Leh
itinerary.content:
After breakfast, begin the journey back to Leh.
Stop at traditional attractions on the way and reach Leh.
Visit Leh market to shop and try Ladakhi food.
Overnight stay at a hotel in Leh.

itinerary.title: Fly back from Leh
itinerary.content:
After breakfast, depart from Leh for your onward journey.
The trip ends here.

importantNotes:
- **Arrive in Leh at least one day before the trip starts.** Under the government SOPs, all travellers must acclimatise in Leh for 48 hours. One day of acclimatisation is included in the package; the extra day before it is your own arrangement, or our team can help you book it.
- If you choose not to arrive a day in advance, we can't be held responsible for any acclimatisation issues. Permits are arranged on the assumption that you arrived one day prior.
- No active physical exertion on your first two days in Leh. Have a light meal on the day you arrive.
- Drink at least 2 to 3 litres of water a day and avoid alcohol, smoking and sedatives.
- The itinerary's advisory is Diamox 250 mg (acetazolamide) twice a day, after breakfast and after dinner, starting at least two days before you travel to Leh and continuing for two days after you arrive. Consult your own doctor before the trip.
- If you notice symptoms of HAPE, HACE or AMS, consult a doctor immediately.
- **Any damage to the bike is borne by the rider.**
- You will be travelling in a high-altitude cold desert with very few medical facilities. We aren't responsible for medical emergencies; we will help arrange logistics if needed, and the expenses are borne by the traveller. Tell us about any existing health issues before you travel.
- Rooms are on triple sharing by default. Twin sharing costs ₹3,000 extra per person and single sharing ₹7,000 extra per person.
- An extra mattress is provided for the third person in triple-sharing rooms.
- Only postpaid mobile connections (Jio, Airtel, BSNL) work in the region.
- Breakfast at the hotel on the last day depends on your departure timing.
- Hotels in Ladakh are more basic than in other parts of the country, and the terrain and weather are harsh and unpredictable.
- Hotels are subject to availability. If a booked hotel is unavailable, you are moved to a comparable property.
- Rates can change if services or hotels change. Any cost increase from changes to the package, such as the number of guests or hotel adjustments, is borne by the traveller.
- The itinerary can change because of weather, road conditions, the physical ability of participants or other disruptions, in the interest of safety, without changing the overall duration of the tour.

faqs.q: Where does the trip start, and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The trip starts and ends in Leh, not Delhi. You reach Leh on your own, and our representative receives you on arrival. We advise arriving at least one day before the trip starts, because the government SOPs require 48 hours of acclimatisation in Leh. You can arrange that extra night yourself or ask our team to help.

faqs.q: What are the travel options and what do they cost?
faqs.a: Per person on triple sharing: Own Bike ₹19,000, Solo Rider ₹32,400, Dual Rider ₹23,400 and SUV / Tempo Traveller ₹24,500. The biking options include the rented bike and fuel as per the itinerary; the SUV / Tempo Traveller option covers the whole route by vehicle, depending on group size. 5% GST is extra.

faqs.q: What do twin and single sharing rooms cost?
faqs.a: Prices are for triple sharing. Twin sharing is ₹3,000 extra per person and single sharing is ₹7,000 extra per person. An extra mattress is provided for the third person in triple-sharing rooms.

7 nights in hotels, camps or cottages and homestays on triple sharing, the meals mentioned in the itinerary, a Himalayan bike for 6 days and fuel as per the itinerary on the biking options (or travel by four-wheeler on the SUV / Tempo Traveller option), a backup vehicle for luggage and repairs, a mechanic with spare parts, knee and elbow guards, inner line permits, the Ladakh Union fee, group pickup and drop, a team captain, an oxygen cylinder in the car, a first-aid kit and a bonfire night.

faqs.q: Are the bike, fuel and riding gear included?
faqs.a: On the biking options, a Himalayan bike for 6 days and fuel as per the itinerary are included, and knee and elbow guards are provided free. Carry your own helmet if you are on a bike. A mechanic with spare parts and a backup vehicle for luggage travel with the group. Any damage to the bike is borne by the rider.

5% GST, meals not specified in the itinerary, entry charges and monument fees, room heater charges, personal expenses and tips, and any cost from unforeseen circumstances such as medical emergencies. Any damage to the bike is borne by the rider.
